newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli charged over Iran chemical arms links.
newsitem.headline: Israeli charged over Iran chemical arms links.

text.p: An Israeli businessman was accused in a Tel Aviv court on Monday of selling Iran equipment for making poison gas, the Justice Ministry said.
Nahum Manbar, who has lived in France since 1985, was arrested in March when he came to Israel for a visit.
Portions of an indictment released by the ministry for publication said that from 1990 to 1995 Manbar, 51, supplied Iran with material for the production of mustard and nerve gas.

The charge sheet presented to the Tel Aviv District Court said the businessman met several times in Europe with Magid Abasfur, identified in the indictment as head of "the Iranian chemical warfare project" and had signed a contract with him.

"In return for supplying the means of production for chemical weapons...the accused received the sum of $16 million from the Iranians," said the indictment, whose release coincided with Israel's annual memorial day for the six million Jews killed in the Nazi Holocaust.
Manbar faces a maximum sentence of life imprisonment if convicted on charges of aiding an enemy of Israel and harming state security. Israel has accused Islamic Iran of seeking its destruction.
Manbar denied in a 1995 interview with the Israeli daily Haaretz that he had supplied Chinese-made material to Iran for the manufacture of poison gas.
Haaretz said last month the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency recently gave Israel information about Manbar's purported connections with Iran and asked it to take action.
In the Haaretz interview, Manbar was quoted as saying he had supplied arms, including tanks, to Iran and had received Israeli Defence Ministry approval for what he exported.
"They (the Iranians) wanted me to build a chemical weapons plant in Iran. All these requests, which appeared suspect to me, I passed on to the proper authorities in Israel," he told Haaretz.
The indictment said Israeli intelligence received information in 1992 that included suspicions about Manbar's alleged chemical weapons dealings with Iran.
"Immediately afterwards, the accused was warned by someone acting on behalf of the intelligence community and pledged to stop immediately all his activities in this area," it said.
"Despite his promise...the accused continued wide-ranging and intensive activities in this sphere until 1994," the charge sheet added.
